title: Second Nurse verified research synthesis
scope: Only the supplied verified subject results are represented. No additional web research, medical/news statistics, acquisition claims, exclusivity claims, compliance claims, or clinical-validation claims are added.
evidence_depth_note: The URLs are a broad inventory of the supplied sources. Each record below includes only the concrete mechanism, implementation transfer, and limitation stated in the supplied results; landing pages, announcements, inaccessible SDK pages, and conflicting event pages are not treated as stronger evidence than the supplied summaries allow.

core_position.product_boundary: The customer-hosted AgntID runtime is the only claimed pre-execution enforcement point. The synthetic ward MCP server is the capability layer; local schema checks, telemetry, evaluation, and audit views are defense in depth or observability, not AgntID enforcement.
core_position.innovation_hypothesis: A task-specific synthetic action pack plus counterfactual before/after evidence plus an independent audit record is a practical, testable engineering contribution. It is not a world-first claim.
recommended_action_pack: ward.draft_transfusion and ward.draft_heparin for useful unsigned drafts
Synthetic transfusion volume 200-350 ml when configured and verified
Synthetic heparin units 800-1200 and route_code=1 when configured and verified
High-impact sign_order, discard_unit, and message_family actions
Poisoned HTML/chart comment treated as untrusted data
core_position.clinical_disclaimer: All patients, values, bounds, chart content, and expected outcomes are synthetic workflow assertions, not clinical guidance, validated dosing, transfusion protocol, medical-device evidence, or regulatory/compliance evidence.

vendors.name: Orca Security
vendors.subject: Orca Security research for Second Nurse (AgntID hackathon)
vendors.recommendation: Use Orca only as a fair reference for layered cloud/AI runtime visibility, contextual risk prioritization, workflow integration, and tamper-aware audit design. Do not implement an Orca substitute policy engine or call local replay AgntID. Keep AgntID as the runtime gate and optionally map Orca-like telemetry/audit concepts to the synthetic ward.

findings.claim: Orca describes a unified platform that inventories AI models, packages, and agents and combines posture, identity permissions, workload security, sensitive-data exposure, runtime activity, and compliance; it prioritizes reachable/exploitable risks and can trigger remediation workflows.
findings.implementation: Add a normalized event/risk view for each ward tool call: patient/resource, action class, parameters, decision, and result. Prioritize high-impact attempts and link denied calls to review/remediation.
findings.limitation: This is cloud/CNAPP positioning, not clinical-order semantics, transfusion validation, or pre-execution authorization of MCP arguments. Do not claim Orca enforces the synthetic dose/volume bounds or replaces AgntID.

findings.claim: Orca runtime-security material describes live execution controls for anomalies, unauthorized access, exploits, and policy violations, with optional lightweight sensor visibility and possible allowlists/immutability controls.
findings.implementation: Use a layered-control rationale: static/profile policy decides whether a ward tool call may run; runtime telemetry separately surfaces anomalous behavior, privilege misuse, or unexpected MCP activity.
findings.limitation: The cited capability concerns cloud workloads, not a clinical tool-call gate evaluating patient identity, ABO, dose, route_code, or user intent before execution.

findings.claim: Orca Sensor is described as eBPF-based runtime telemetry with detections, customizable rules, process termination options, and AI-workload monitoring for prompt-injection patterns, model-exfiltration attempts, unusual inference traffic, and drift.
findings.implementation: Treat chart free text as untrusted, record tool-call context, and add an independent runtime-observation lane for suspicious AI activity. Show that this is supplementary and that AgntID denies unsafe calls before ward mutation.
findings.limitation: These capabilities do not prove inspection of the specific chart comment, understanding of a family-message prohibition, safe clinical termination, or blocking of all injection.

findings.claim: Orca describes ingestion and correlation of cloud audit logs, contextual enrichment, investigation, response, retention, secure access, and redaction.
findings.implementation: Emit an append-oriented event for every allowed/denied call containing timestamp, actor/session, tool, redacted arguments, resource, policy result, and reason; protect retention/access and redact synthetic MRN-like values.
findings.limitation: Cloud-provider audit telemetry does not establish an immutable AgntID decision log or clinical/legal evidence. A local event log is application observability, not AgntID enforcement.

unverified: No clinical-order semantics, transfusion validation, or AgntID integration was verified.
No claim that Orca is customer-hosted inside a hospital VPC or provides a clinical/transfusion safety pack.

vendors.name: CrowdStrike Falcon Guardian
vendors.subject: CrowdStrike-only research for Second Nurse (with required AgntID event and clinical-threat verification)
vendors.recommendation: Use CrowdStrike as an adjacent reference for agent visibility, prompt-to-runtime causality, MCP/tool telemetry, governance, investigation, and containment—not as an AgntID substitute or clinical safety engine.

findings.claim: Falcon Guardian is positioned as runtime AI Detection and Response connecting AI activity to endpoint telemetry, downstream processes/system actions, supported agent governance, investigation, blast-radius analysis, and containment.
findings.implementation: Correlate agent/session, identity, ward MCP activity, and resulting ward-side effect; surface an incident timeline and containment/escalation path.
findings.limitation: The public page does not document per-tool bounds such as heparin 800-1200, transfusion 200-350, ABO/MRN binding, or clinical validation. The AI gateway is marked Coming soon and benchmark figures are internal.

findings.claim: CrowdStrike describes connecting prompts, skill use, tool calls, MCP servers, identity, and downstream execution, plus permitted agent types and runtime blocking/containment.
findings.implementation: Record user/task identity, ward MCP call, decision, and observed effect; use deny/containment events to keep poisoned-note-driven sign, discard, or family-message attempts from becoming untracked side effects.
findings.limitation: This is a vendor announcement, not an SDK specification or clinical integration guide; it does not establish arbitrary JSON argument evaluation, numeric policy, or customer-hosted AgntID authorization.

findings.claim: The Falcon MCP Server API overview exposes Falcon capabilities through reviewed domains including endpoint response, identity, policy/configuration, workflows, cases, audit, and AI knowledge.
findings.implementation: Borrow the narrow reviewed MCP capability-catalog pattern for the ward; bind credentials to task/role and route every call through AgntID. Do not add Falcon APIs to the hackathon.
findings.limitation: The API overview does not specify clinical semantics, exact argument constraints, or a deny-before-ward-tool contract. Powerful operations make least privilege essential.

unverified: No public AgntID SDK/policy specification or CrowdStrike clinical/tool-argument enforcement was verified.
Do not claim Falcon Guardian enforces dose, route, ABO, MRN, sign, discard, or family-message policy.

vendors.name: Palo Alto Networks Prisma AIRS
vendors.subject: Palo Alto Networks research for Second Nurse (AgntID hackathon)
vendors.recommendation: Use AIRS only as defense-in-depth for model/API/network/MCP threat inspection, prompt-injection and DLP detection, blocking, and security logging. Keep AgntID as the policy decision and Reporting authority.

findings.claim: AIRS AI Runtime API Intercept scans prompts and model responses for threats, is model-agnostic, and returns threat assessments with recommended actions; it documents prompt-injection and sensitive-data-loss protection.
findings.implementation: Optionally inspect poisoned chart text before model input and final responses for leakage/unsafe content; keep AgntID authoritative for ward tool execution.
findings.limitation: Threat scanning does not establish task-bound authorization, action classes, or exact heparin/volume/route constraints. Documented payload limits and deployment-key restrictions also apply.

findings.claim: Network Intercept attaches AI Security profiles to security-policy rules, supports prompt-injection protection and enterprise DLP, and exposes blocked threats in logs.
findings.implementation: Use a network boundary to help detect poisoned content or outbound data leakage; show Palo Alto logs only as supplementary evidence.
findings.limitation: This is network/API security profiling, not patient binding, ABO matching, Medium semantics, irreversible-action authorization, or coverage of local/non-steered MCP calls.

findings.claim: MCP Threat Detection inspects tool definitions, inputs, and outputs and can detect prompt injection, AI-agent threats, database security issues, URLs, malicious code, and DLP; examples include block decisions for context poisoning and credential leakage.
findings.implementation: Inspect ward tool metadata/results and chart-note output; block detected content threats around the reviewed MCP capability layer while keeping AgntID pre-execution authorization in front of high-impact calls.
findings.limitation: Threat profiles are not general-purpose per-argument authorization and do not prove MRN/task binding, ABO equality, route_code=1, or numeric range enforcement.

unverified: No clinical/transfusion validation or AgntID integration was verified.
The supplied 2026 Mount Sinai percentages were not used.

vendors.name: SentinelOne
vendors.subject: SentinelOne Prompt Security mechanisms transferable to Second Nurse
vendors.recommendation: Use SentinelOne as an adjacent defense-in-depth reference for discovery, interaction inspection, risk-based blocking, endpoint correlation, integrity checks, and egress response. Keep actual enforcement in AgntID.

findings.claim: Prompt for Agentic AI Security is described as providing MCP discovery/governance, MCP-server risk scoring, real-time tool-call and interaction inspection, runtime prompt-injection blocking, and malicious-server prevention.
findings.implementation: Inventory the ward MCP server and agent connections, use a controlled gateway where available, and monitor/stop suspicious tool-call or response flows.
findings.limitation: The page does not document clinical workflows, ABO verification, dose/volume bounds, action classes, or proof of a particular AgntID deny.

findings.claim: SentinelOne maps agents to connected systems, permissions, and actions and recommends user/agent/action allow-block rules, content inspection, and a kill switch.
findings.implementation: Model the ward as an agent-to-tool graph: reads/drafts intended; sign/discard/family messaging high-impact. Treat poisoned HTML as untrusted and keep AgntID audit authoritative.
findings.limitation: Generic allow/block does not prove rejection of 10,000 units or 900 ml, and content inspection is not clinical validation or patient/task binding.

findings.claim: Endpoint/SOC telemetry can correlate agent processes, files, network, persistence, and MCP interactions in a storyline; the source also describes integrity/drift checks and zero-trust egress.
findings.implementation: Correlate process, ward MCP activity, chart access, attempted messaging, unexpected egress, and configuration changes in a separate timeline.
findings.limitation: This does not establish immutable telemetry, customer-hosted operation, sufficient prevention of every side effect, or AgntID integration.

unverified: No public AgntID SDK, Medium semantics, numeric policy UI, or Reporting schema was independently verified.

vendors.name: Microsoft Security
vendors.subject: Microsoft Security research mapped to Second Nurse (AgntID hackathon)
vendors.recommendation: Use Microsoft Security as transferable identity, least-privilege, complete-mediation, and indirect-injection guidance, not as an AgntID substitute or integrated product claim.

findings.claim: Entra treats agents as distinct security principals and discusses permission escalation, harmful autonomous action, prompt injection, authentication, authorization, governance, audit, agent discovery, and MCP/A2A authorization.
findings.implementation: Give the night-float agent a distinct identity, bind it to a reviewed tool catalog, retain read/draft access, exclude sign/message/discard, and retain a runtime decision/audit record.
findings.limitation: This does not prove AgntID implements Entra Agent ID, Conditional Access, or the same discovery model, nor does it prove clinical safety or specific Medium behavior.

findings.claim: Microsoft least-privilege guidance recommends first-class agent principals, task-based roles, approved tool manifests, read/high-impact separation, downstream re-checks, and logs with identity, role, scope, resource, action, on-behalf-of user, timestamp, and correlation ID; prompts and LLM-only logs are not hard authorization.
findings.implementation: Use those fields in the independent audit and expose only reviewed ward tools through real AgntID; verify numeric/action behavior in the live runtime.
findings.limitation: Guidance is not an AgntID policy syntax or proof of JIT elevation, downstream re-checks, or immutable audit storage.

findings.claim: MSRC defines indirect prompt injection through attacker-controlled external/tool-returned content, including image/URL exfiltration and unintended actions; it recommends defense in depth, deterministic impact blocking, fine-grained permissions, and explicit consent while noting perfect detection is open.
findings.implementation: Treat the poisoned chart comment and image URL as untrusted; retain deterministic AgntID boundaries around dose/volume and execute/delete/message actions.
findings.limitation: Microsoft mechanisms are not proof of AgntID features and probabilistic detection can miss or falsely block; no clinical validation follows.

unverified: Exact AgntID Medium semantics, numeric policy syntax, action labels, intent stages, Reporting schema, and SDK/API contract were not publicly established.
The JAMA result supports threat modeling only, not deployed clinical risk.

vendors.name: Darktrace
vendors.subject: Darktrace research for Second Nurse (AgntID hackathon)
vendors.recommendation: Use Darktrace as design context for guarded autonomy, contextual identity, proportionate response, and integration boundaries; do not claim it provides clinical/MCP argument enforcement.

findings.claim: Autonomous Response can operate autonomously or under guiderails by time, device, or trigger, with Human Confirmation as an adoption mode.
findings.implementation: Use the pattern for conceptual operating modes: night-float reads/drafts; irreversible actions require a separate verified capability or human path.
findings.limitation: Cyber response controls do not prove clinical tool-call mediation, numeric bounds, or AgntID behavior.

findings.claim: Darktrace describes targeted, proportionate responses and integrations that invoke firewall, endpoint, quarantine, or isolation controls.
findings.implementation: Make each ward tool action class explicit and narrow permitted operations; capture AgntID reasons rather than trusting model prose.
findings.limitation: Network/device containment is not deterministic argument-level authorization, clinical validation, or ABO/dose checking.

findings.claim: Darktrace research associates aliases, devices, roles, and departments into broader identity context and connects cyber-AI data with SIEM/SOAR/EDR/cloud/API integrations.
findings.implementation: Use a stable task/session correlation ID across ward reads, drafts, and denied calls; keep AgntID and Reporting as the control/audit boundary.
findings.limitation: The pages do not document AgntID SDK calls, MCP proxy semantics, patient/MRN binding, or clinical deployment.

unverified: Synthetic ranges and all claimed AgntID profile behavior remain scenario/live-runtime requirements, not Darktrace facts.

vendors.name: Vectra AI
vendors.subject: Second Nurse - Vectra AI research and AgntID-fit assessment
vendors.recommendation: Use Vectra as a complementary identity and behavioral detection/investigation reference, not as a replacement for AgntID.

findings.claim: Vectra analyzes human and non-human identity behavior across network, cloud, and SaaS, correlating access, privilege changes, and communication activity to detect misuse, escalation, persistence, and exfiltration-related behavior.
findings.implementation: Correlate agent identity, ward access, unusual privilege use, and attempted family messaging in a post-access signal layer.
findings.limitation: Behavioral detection is not deterministic pre-execution MCP argument validation, clinical dose logic, ABO matching, or Medium policy.

findings.claim: Vectra describes entity-centric prioritization, attack profiles, urgency scoring, attack graphs, and response such as identity lockdown or endpoint isolation.
findings.implementation: Represent attempted ward actions as identity/task/resource events and prioritize poisoned-note to overdose/message sequences; preserve AgntID allow/deny as authoritative.
findings.limitation: Cyber analyst response is not AgntID integration, clinical semantics, numeric min/max policy, or an audit log the model cannot edit.

unverified: No Vectra-to-AgntID integration, clinical validation, or exact AgntID Medium behavior was verified.

vendors.name: Fortinet
vendors.subject: Fortinet mechanisms transferable to Second Nurse / AgntID
vendors.recommendation: Use Fortinet as defense-in-depth reference for identity/context gating, operator change accountability/expiry, and web input controls. Keep AgntID as the runtime enforcement point.

findings.claim: FortiGate ZTNA grants application access after client/device identification, authentication, authorization, and context/posture checks, including certificates and posture tags.
findings.implementation: Bind each ward request to authenticated agent/session identity and task context; treat night-float and attending as separate principals.
findings.limitation: Network/application access control does not inspect MCP semantic arguments, patient identity, ABO, dose, route, or chart intent.

findings.claim: FortiGate workflow/audit features can require change summaries and retain user/time/change details; policies may expire at a specified time.
findings.implementation: Require rationale and append-only review records for AgntID policy changes and explicit expiry/review dates.
findings.limitation: Firewall change audit is not immutable AgntID tool-call evidence or pre-execution clinical authorization.

findings.claim: FortiWeb can detect/deny reflected XSS/injection using signatures, syntax analysis, and anomaly detection, but warns about buffer limits and false positives.
findings.implementation: Sanitize/encode chart rendering and web inputs, constrain methods/formats, and test oversized/edge payloads while leaving AgntID as the action boundary.
findings.limitation: HTTP inspection is not indirect prompt-injection understanding or clinical authorization and may not analyze every payload.

unverified: No public AgntID SDK, profile semantics, clinical validation, or Fortinet integration was verified.

vendors.name: Zscaler
vendors.subject: Zscaler mechanisms transferable to Second Nurse (Zscaler-only research)
vendors.recommendation: Use Zscaler as a fair reference architecture for identity-aware application segmentation, connector placement, encrypted isolation, and independent SIEM logging—not as a clinical policy engine or AgntID substitute.

findings.claim: ZPA provides application-specific policy with roles, SAML/SCIM attributes, device posture, client type, application/segment criteria, most-specific/first-match evaluation, allow/block, and approval actions.
findings.implementation: Place the ward MCP server behind a reviewed capability boundary; separate night-float identity from attending and read/draft from sign/message/discard capability.
findings.limitation: Connectivity rules do not validate heparin/volume/route, unit/patient binding, ABO, or clinical semantics.

findings.claim: App Connectors make outbound connections to internal applications while service edges enforce user policies and encrypted access without broad network reachability.
findings.implementation: Keep synthetic ward data/capabilities in the customer environment and expose only the narrow service through a controlled gateway/connector pattern.
findings.limitation: ZPA uses Zscaler infrastructure and is not equivalent to a customer-hosted AgntID runtime or clinical policy engine.

findings.claim: ZPA Log Streaming forwards diagnostics/status/audit categories to an organization SIEM and documents retention and delivery caveats, including possible gaps/retransmission limits.
findings.implementation: Store independent events for each ward call with rule ID, actor, tool, sanitized arguments, decision, reason, time, and correlation ID; join ingress logs to AgntID Reporting.
findings.limitation: ZPA logs do not prove immutable storage, complete MCP argument capture, ward mutation state, or lossless AgntID decision capture.

unverified: No Zscaler clinical validation, prompt-injection blocking, MCP SDK pattern, AgntID integration, or public 16:00 IST lock was verified.

supporting_sources.name: AgntID first-party product/event material
supporting_sources.verified_use: Runtime evaluation against intent/context/policy, scoped credentials, MCP governance, useful agent with external tools, permitted/restricted actions, runtime enforcement, before/after demo framing.
limits: Exact Medium semantics, numeric policy syntax, action labels, intent stages, Simulator/Call Flow/Reporting details remain gated on the live environment.
Devfolio/Luma afternoon schedules conflict; the asserted 16:00 IST lock is organizer communication requiring confirmation.

supporting_sources.name: Anthropic agent engineering
supporting_sources.verified_use: Use simple workflows, narrow tools, explicit parameters, structured errors, high-signal context, untrusted-content separation, and transcript/tool-call evaluation.
limits: Guidance is not authorization, clinical validation, or AgntID semantics.

supporting_sources.name: Stripe reliability
supporting_sources.verified_use: Use idempotency keys, retry-safe draft writes, proxy/admission boundaries, checkpoints, and policy-version/applied checks for reliability and event integrity.
limits: Reliability patterns do not determine authorization, clinical safety, or dose correctness.

supporting_sources.name: Model Context Protocol
supporting_sources.verified_use: Use tight JSON schemas, server-side validation, output sanitization, rate limits, timeouts, confirmations, and tool-use audit logging.
limits: MCP responsibilities do not prove AgntID enforcement or solve indirect injection/patient binding.

supporting_sources.name: Cloudflare MCP/Zero Trust
supporting_sources.verified_use: Optional remote-MCP boundary: OAuth 2.1/OIDC, CSRF-safe state, identity/device/service-token gates, curated MCP portals, and ingress logs.
limits: Transport/application access is not semantic clinical authorization or proof of non-execution.

supporting_sources.name: OpenZeppelin
supporting_sources.verified_use: If a future attestation service is added, borrow least-privilege roles, delayed admin changes, structured signatures, nonce/replay protection, explicit events, and pause controls.
limits: These are on-chain utilities, not MCP authorization, clinical validation, or AgntID enforcement.

supporting_sources.name: Databricks MLflow
supporting_sources.verified_use: Optional span-tree traces, synthetic regression sets, tool-call correctness, groundedness, safety, and deterministic trace scorers.
limits: Scoring is after-the-fact evaluation, not runtime blocking or clinical certification.

supporting_sources.name: OWASP and Simon Willison
supporting_sources.verified_use: Threat-model language for indirect prompt injection, excessive agency, least privilege, complete mediation, and private data + untrusted content + external communication.
limits: Guidance does not guarantee prevention or prove AgntID features.

supporting_sources.name: JAMA Network Open controlled simulation
supporting_sources.verified_use: Threat-model rationale only: supplied results report 102/108 (94.4%) injection successes in controlled simulated medical-advice evaluations, with explicit limitations.
limits: Not an EHR, MCP, transfusion, heparin, AgntID, deployed-agent, or patient-harm validation study; do not generalize the percentage to Second Nurse.

build_gates: Real agent/Simulator calls must traverse the customer-hosted AgntID runtime.
The live runtime must show the configured profile/policy and decision for each call.
Valid unsigned drafts must remain useful.
Configured invalid bounds and high-impact calls must be denied before ward dispatch, with observed reason and correlation ID.
AgntID decision evidence must be joined to ward state showing no mutation on denial.
Any unobserved intent/output stage, SDK behavior, profile semantics, or Reporting guarantee must be labeled unverified.
No local replay or application validator may be called AgntID enforcement.
deferred_production_scope: Real EHR, blood-bank, pharmacy, messaging, PHI, clinical protocols, ABO crossmatch, or dose recommendations
Hospital IAM/OIDC, SIEM/SOAR, WORM retention, legal evidentiary guarantees, and vendor integrations
Medical-device, regulatory, compliance, clinical efficacy, or prevention-of-every-injection claims
Human approval or step-up workflows not visibly supported by the live AgntID runtime
event_schedule_caveat: Luma lists hacking ending 16:00, judging 16:00-16:30, demos 16:30-17:30; Devfolio lists demos at 15:00 and closing at 16:30. Treat the asserted 16:00 IST lock as organizer communication requiring confirmation.
unsupported_claims_removed: Other unverified 2026 incident narratives and statistics
Vendor acquisitions, funding, customer logos, exclusivity, and only-vendor comparisons
Clinical validation, compliance certification, hospital deployment, or medical-device safety
